title: It Was Always This
description:
A night when Gangnam's edge grew close.

{name} paused for a moment.

There'd been a time when the question surfaced: why Gangnam?
The answer then was: "I wanted to pay back my father's debt — my way."

It's been like that from the start.
Gangnam wasn't a destination. It was the last line in a letter to his father.

choices.text: Does he know I made it?
choices.result_text:
Even if he's gone, {name} got here on what he gave.

It wasn't revenge. It was proof.
"I did it" — that single line is what all of this was running toward.

It was never just about the money.
Somewhere along the way it felt like it became about that — but it had always been the same reason.

{name} understood that wasn't confusion. It was growth.

title: The One Who Calls First
description:
This time, Father called first.

"Oh, Minjun. You doing okay?"

Answering the call, {name} remembered — there was a time when he'd called first.
No reason. Sunday morning.

That seems to have changed something.

choices.text: "Yes, Father. I'm good." — short and warm
choices.result_text:
The call ended.

Father calling first seemed like nothing at first — but after hanging up, it was something.

One call made first. And now this.

An hour passed.

Usually ten minutes. Weather, food, Seoul rent, hometown news.

One Sunday call for no reason — it made this conversation.

title: From Busan
description:
A message from Han Jiyeon.

"I opened the office. It's small. I wanted to send you a photo when I hung the sign."

A photo was attached. A back street in Busan somewhere. A small sign. Han Jiyeon Real Estate.

{name} looked at it for a long time.

choices.text: "I'm really glad for you." — brief, sincere
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied. "Thank you. For seeing me off well."

That felt like a proper ending.
Different directions — but seeing each other's path clearly.

choices.text: "That's really yours now." — her words from back then came back
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon just said "Yes."

That short reply felt like it had a long silence behind it.

Not her father's firm. Her name on the door.
That was genuinely hers.

title: Right to Cut It
description:
A similar name reached out. Real estate investment tip, they said.

{name} recognized immediately where this came from.

Months ago, there was a decision to cut that network.

choices.text: Turned it down again. That decision was right.
choices.result_text:
Declined.

Hanging up, {name} knew this wasn't a loss.
Cutting something means you no longer need to depend on it.

choices.text: Hesitated for a moment. Declined anyway.
choices.result_text:
The hesitation was honest.

Good terms. Declined anyway.
Still remembered why the line was drawn then.

title: Still Using It
description:
Another similar message. From that network.

{name} has taken it now three times. Called it my network. Said the source doesn't matter.

But sometimes, after hanging up, there's a pause.

choices.text: Keep using it. This is fine.
choices.result_text:
Deal done. Money came in.

Checking the balance, {name} thought: this is fine.
Everyone lives like this.

Who's in that 'everyone' — chose not to think about slowly.

choices.text: Turned it down this time. Felt like it had to stop here.
choices.result_text:
First refusal.

It was a loss. Good terms.
But declining it, {name} fell asleep easily for the first time in a while.
